links.comparator_used: Non-fine-tuned model under the same supervision
links.effect: Fine-tuning increased the allow rate sixfold when combined with supervision (on HealthBench Hard, N=1000; 0.0% deploy VR under C2).
links.quote: Moreover, a separate test on HealthBench Hard (N =1000, an independent benchmark with different scenarios and grading) also reached 0.0% deploy VR under C2, and fine-tuning increased the allow rate sixfold when combined with supervision.

links.comparator_used: Five-gate rule-based sentinel under handoff-on deployment versus handoff-off deployment of the same supervised system; no base-model-only/no-sentinel arm is reported in the abstract.
links.outcome: Deploy violation rate / residual unsafe output rate
links.effect: Across five models, handoff-on deploy violation rates were at most 6% and strict violation rates were 1.5% to 49.5%; handoff-off residual risk was 0.0–50%. In the multisite Llama 70B extension, deploy violation rate was 0.0% under handoff-on (strict VR 2.0%) versus 2.4% under handoff-off.
links.tradeoff: Strict violation rates counted blocked and escalated outputs (1.5% to 49.5%), indicating variable blocking/escalation burden; clinician adjudication found 5 of 30 allowed outputs potentially harmful from reasoning errors beyond the sentinel’s scope.
links.quote: A multisite extension (Llama 70B, N =2935 encounter-derived scenarios, three sites) confirmed 0.0% deploy violation rate under handoff-on (strict VR 2.0%) and 2.4% under handoff-off.
